# Garry Kasparov Summary
Garry Kasparov was involved in notable matches against IBM supercomputers, including a 1996 contest with Deep Blue, which he won (4–2), and a subsequent match in 1997 that Deep Blue won (3½–2½); this latter match was the first defeat of a reigning world champion by a computer under tournament conditions. He also participated in a 1999 game against "Kasparov versus the World," which he won after 62 moves. Later engagements included a six-game match against Deep Junior in January 2003, which ended in a draw after Kasparov offered a draw in the final game, and a four-game match against the computer program X3D Fritz in November 2003, which also ended in a draw.
Beyond chess, Kasparov became politically active. He announced his candidacy for World Chess Federation president in 2013 but lost the election in 2014, after which he was found guilty of violating the FIDE Code of Ethics. He has been a vocal political critic of the Russian government, speaking out against the invasion of Ukraine and calling for the fall of Putin's regime. He has faced state repercussions, including being designated a "foreign agent" and being placed on a list of "terrorists and extremists" by Russia.
